title: Eddie Durham and wishing he played classical guitar
summary: Goodwin patterned himself on Eddie Durham and would trade everything to be a classical guitarist like Segovia.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well tell me, how about people like Teddy Bunn and Freddie Green? I mean, was there a bigtime guitarist when you were coming along?
Eddie Durham.
Eddie Durham, he was a guy that you picked up on?
Yeah, he's the guy that I sort of patterned from.
On guitar?
On guitar.
How about classical guitar. Do you listen very much to Segovia?
Very beautiful.
I know he is, but do you listen to him?
Everytime I can. Everytime he --
Do you have albums of his?
No I don't have.
But you go and hear him or if he's on --
I have heard him several times on tv.
In your opinion, what is the biggest difference between a classical guitar and the jazz guitar? I mean simple now, quick and easy.
Well, I just wish I was a classical guitar player because I think it's the most beautiful thing in the world.
Well, the way you play guitar, I think is very beautiful.

Well I would trade everything I know and everything I could learn in the next 20 years for -- just to be a classical guitar player because I think it's -- you know, you see it played. It's a difficult thing to do but guitar is difficult, period.
You would have had to spend your whole life on that.
Well --
No way you could become a classical
guitarist now.
No way, no. There are so many things that I'd have to learn over.
Well you're one hell of a guitarist, that I know and the best vocalist I've ever heard.
Well classical guitar would be my bag if I had started on it when I was very young. See, I was nearly grown when I started into music so this is in itself --
Well this is an interesting comment, it really is, Crook. Well, let's go on with this excellent outline. Yeah, Baby?
